This sentence is bursting at the punctuation marks with news of the dire import of self-reference as applied to sentences, a practice that could prove to be a veritable Pandora's box of potential havoc, for if a sentence can refer or allude to itself, why not a lowly subordinate clause, perhaps this very clause ? First, though, I would like to mention an amusing incident. When Lee Sallows' self-documenting sentence was to be printed in the narrow columns of Scientific American, nobody remembered to tell the typesetters not to break any unhyphenated words. As luck would have it, two such breaks were introduced, yielding two spurious hyphens, thus spoiling (in a superficial sense) the accuracy of his construction. How subtly one can get snagged when self-reference is concerned!
